theme: FRED / BEA / BLS / Census API clients and curated macro panels (consumer sentiment, PCE services, CPI lodging, airfares, unemployment by metro)
queries_run: fredapi github python client FRED economic data
bea api python github client BEA data
bls api python github client BLS data

candidates.name: Opportunity Insights Economic Tracker
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed CSVs (data dictionary, data documentation, data revisions log) behind tracktherecovery.org: county- and state-level daily/weekly consumer spending (by credit/debit card processors, broken out by category incl. restaurants/entertainment/travel-adjacent spend), small-business revenue, employment by industry and income quartile, job postings; national series run 2020-present, still updated; 1,892 commits on main.
candidates.why_useful: Directly named in CONTEXT.md gap #6 ('Opportunity Insights Economic Tracker card spend'); a real, freely licensed, granular (county) consumer-spend panel that reads on discretionary/travel spending, useful as a high-frequency consumer-strength cross-check for nights/ADR regional splits.
candidates.license: Free with attribution to data providers + academic paper
candidates.last_activity: not resolved exactly; repo actively maintained (1,892 commits)
candidates.size_hint: multiple CSVs, county x day/week granularity

candidates.name: pegeler/unemployment (LAUS annual averages)
candidates.what_it_holds: R package bundling BLS Local Area Unemployment Statistics (LAUS) annual averages 1990-2017 as a data.frame: 90,088 rows x 9 columns (LAUS code, state/county FIPS, county name, year, labor force, employment, unemployment level, unemployment rate) at county/metro-area level.
candidates.why_useful: Fills the 'unemployment by metro' curated-panel ask directly: county-level history back to 1990 committed as data, no API key needed, usable as a regional consumer-strength control for NA nights/ADR.

candidates.name: blscrapeR
candidates.what_it_holds: R package/API client wrapping the BLS API: state- and metro-area unemployment (LAUS) via county_fips()/quick_unemp_rate(), CPI/inflation adjustment functions using CPI data from 1947 onward (inflation_adjust()), quick_employed_level(), quick_laborForce_rate(); CRAN package, 381 commits, actively maintained.
candidates.why_useful: One-command pull for metro unemployment and long-run CPI (1947+) matching the theme's 'unemployment by metro' and 'CPI' asks; more turnkey than raw BLS API for regional consumer-strength splits (NA/EMEA proxy via US metro cuts).
candidates.time_coverage: CPI from 1947; unemployment current + historical via API
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps our existing BLS CPI holding; adds LAUS metro convenience layer

candidates.name: palewire/cpi
candidates.what_it_holds: Python package (145 stars, MIT) with a /data directory bundling CPI series for inflation adjustment (US dollars any-year-to-any-year); pip-installable, docs at palewi.re/docs/cpi/.
candidates.why_useful: Turnkey CPI deflator library with data actually committed to the repo rather than fetched live each time, useful for point-in-time-safe inflation adjustment of any nominal series in the model (ADR, GBV) without hitting BLS API rate limits.
candidates.size_hint: small (CPI index only, not itemized subcomponents like lodging)

candidates.name: beaapi (official US BEA Python client)
candidates.what_it_holds: Official BEA-maintained Python package (pip install beaapi, CC0) wrapping the full BEA API: NIPA tables (incl. PCE services detail), international transactions, GDP-by-industry, regional economic accounts; includes automatic rate-limit throttling (100 req/min, 100MB/min) and caches metadata locally.
candidates.why_useful: Official, well-throttled client for pulling PCE services / travel-related NIPA line items programmatically and repeatably for the PCE travel panel already held; useful for extending or re-verifying that panel with fresh vintages.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: overlaps existing BEA PCE travel panel; adds official, throttled client

candidates.name: fredapi
candidates.what_it_holds: Widely-used Python wrapper (Apache-2.0, 67 commits) for FRED and ALFRED (Archival FRED); supports pulling historical point-in-time vintages/revisions of any FRED series via get_series_as_of_date / realtime parameters, returned as pandas Series/DataFrames.
candidates.why_useful: Directly supports gap #4 (ALFRED-style macro vintages / point-in-time series) since it exposes ALFRED's real-time revision history, not just the latest print, for any of the ~40 FRED series already tracked (CPI, PCE, sentiment).
candidates.geography: US (whatever FRED covers, incl. some international)
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: we already pull FRED; this specifically unlocks ALFRED vintages we may not be using

candidates.name: fedfred
candidates.what_it_holds: Listed on the GitHub 'fred-api' topic as a 'feature-rich Python package for Federal Reserve economic database interaction'; direct repo fetch returned 404 at the guessed path so the exact owner/URL needs re-verification via the topic page rather than the guessed slug.
candidates.why_useful: Potential alternative/more full-featured FRED client (worth a follow-up scout with the correct owner slug); flagged here as unresolved rather than dropped since it appeared in the official GitHub topic listing.

candidates.name: datamade/census
candidates.what_it_holds: Popular Python wrapper (682 stars, BSD-3) for the US Census Bureau API: ACS and SF1 datasets, redistricting data, geography lookups via integration with the `us` package; no committed data, requires a free Census API key.
candidates.why_useful: Turnkey client for pulling ACS demographic/housing/income data by metro, which underlies household-formation and travel-propensity proxies and could support regional consumer-strength or long-term-rental (housing) cross-checks.

candidates.name: censusapi (R)
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (257 commits) giving lightweight access to 1,500+ Census Bureau API endpoints (ACS, and many lesser-known surveys) via getCensus()/listCensusApis()/listCensusMetadata().
candidates.why_useful: Broadest-coverage Census client found (1,500+ endpoints beyond just ACS), useful if the team wants Census Bureau series beyond ACS (e.g. Business Formation Statistics, Household Pulse Survey) for consumer-strength or housing-supply proxies.

candidates.name: census-api-datasets
candidates.what_it_holds: Tracks additions/removals of datasets on the Census Bureau's API over time (a changelog/registry, 15 stars) — i.e., a curated index of what's available and when it appeared or disappeared from the API.
candidates.why_useful: Metadata tool for discovering new/deprecated Census series systematically rather than manually; low direct KPI value but useful for a future systematic scan of Census offerings relevant to travel/housing.

candidates.name: bls (Python, OliverSherouse)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python client (GPL-2.0, dev branch 54 commits) wrapping the BLS API; get_series() pulls any BLS series ID with API-key-gated multi-decade history vs a default 3-year window with no key.
candidates.why_useful: Simple alternative BLS client for pulling CPI lodging/airfares/employment series programmatically and repeatably; marginal over what the team already has via FRED's BLS mirror, but useful if BLS-only series (not on FRED) are needed.
candidates.time_coverage: up to full BLS history with API key

candidates.name: hub-delay-audit
candidates.what_it_holds: Analysis pipeline (not committed data) pointing to BTS On-Time Performance (583,985 flight rows, Jan 2019) and BTS DB1B Coupon Survey (9,846,816 itinerary rows, Q1 2019, 10% sample of domestic itineraries) from transtats.bts.gov; studies minimum-connection-time standards at US hub airports.
candidates.why_useful: Concretely documents the BTS DB1B/On-Time pull method named in gap #10 (airline capacity/traffic); a working reference pipeline for grabbing DB1B itinerary-level data even though the raw files themselves aren't committed.

candidates.name: us-flight-delays-eda
candidates.what_it_holds: EDA of BTS Reporting Carrier On-Time Performance data: raw source has ~2,000,000 domestic flight rows spanning 1987-2020 (not committed, gitignored as airline_2m.csv), analysis subset ~644K flights 2010-2019 across 22 carriers.
candidates.why_useful: Another documented, reproducible method for pulling long-run (1987-2020) BTS domestic flight volume data, relevant as a US air-travel-demand proxy for the travel-volume/capacity gap; data itself must be re-pulled from BTS directly.

candidates.name: Rdatasets
candidates.what_it_holds: Mirror of 3,648 datasets originally bundled inside R packages, exported as CSV and Parquet with an HTML/CSV index; broad general-purpose collection (economics, social science, biology, etc.), not macro-specific but includes many economic/time-series teaching datasets.
candidates.why_useful: Worth a targeted grep of its CSV index for any macro/travel/tourism/airfare series bundled from lesser-known R packages (e.g. AER, Ecdat, wooldridge) that might not otherwise surface; low direct hit rate but essentially free to check.
candidates.license: GPL-3.0 (code); data licensing uncertain per maintainer's own disclosure

candidates.name: fbi (factor-based imputation, FRED-MD/QD vignette)
candidates.what_it_holds: R package (GPL-3.0, 70 commits) implementing Bai-Ng-style factor/matrix-completion imputation for high-dimensional macro panels; ships a vignette applying the method to the FRED-MD monthly macro dataset (McCracken & Ng), though the FRED-MD data itself is fetched externally, not committed.
candidates.why_useful: Points to FRED-MD/FRED-QD (large curated 100+ series monthly/quarterly macro panels, standard in macro-nowcasting) as an external target, plus a working imputation method for handling ragged-edge/missing macro data in a MIDAS/DFM nowcast — relevant to gap #17 (mixed-frequency nowcasting methods).

notes: WebSearch tool exhausted its session-wide quota (200/200) before this scout could run any queries directly, despite following the assigned MODALITY; all findings above come from WebFetch against GitHub repo pages, topic-tag pages, and one raw README, using known repo names from prior knowledge as seeds instead of fresh search discovery. github.com/search (the actual search endpoint) also 429'd after one attempt and was avoided thereafter -- topic pages (github.com/topics/<tag>) worked as a substitute and are the main discovery mechanism used here. Because search was unavailable, coverage of BEA-specific and airfare-specific curated panels is thin (only one bea-api-tagged repo exists on GitHub, last updated 2017) -- a follow-up scout with working WebSearch should re-run 'BEA regional PCE github', 'university of michigan consumer sentiment scraper github', 'airfare index CPI github dataset', and 'FRED-MD FRED-QD github mirror csv' once quota resets. The strongest concrete hit is OpportunityInsights/EconomicTracker, which is explicitly named in CONTEXT.md gap #6 and is a real, actively-updated, county-level dataset (not just a client) -- worth a dedicated close look at its data dictionary for a travel/hospitality spending cut. No FRED-MD/FRED-QD mirror repository with the actual committed CSV panel was found/verified (only tooling that consumes it) -- this remains open and is probably the single highest-value target left for a Sonnet-model deep-dive with a live gh or WebSearch budget, since FRED-MD/QD is exactly the ALFRED-adjacent vintage-macro-panel gap #4 describes.
